stem:
The three substances shown all have some acidic properties.

{{figure:pdf_visual_01.png}}

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Write an equation for the reaction between propan-1-ol and sodium metal.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: Give the order of the relative acidities of propanoic acid, propan-1-ol and phenol, stating the most acidic first.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Methanoic acid, $\text{HCO}_2\text{H}$, has a similar acid strength to propanoic acid.

Describe a chemical test to distinguish between these two acids. Name the acid which gives a positive result in this test and describe the observations that would be made.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
The ester phenyl propanoate, $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{CO}_2\text{C}_6\text{H}_5$, can be made from phenol and propanoic acid in a **two-step** synthesis. The first step produces an acyl chloride.

For this **two-step** synthesis,

- draw the structure of the product of the first step,
- state the reagents and conditions needed for each step of the synthesis.

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem:
An unknown compound, $\mathbf{Z}$, is propan-1-ol, propanal or propanoic acid. The proton NMR spectrum of $\mathbf{Z}$ dissolved in $\text{CDCl}_3$ is shown.

{{figure:pdf_visual_02.png}}

parts.label: (e)(i)
parts.text: From the proton NMR spectrum, identify $\mathbf{Z}$.

parts.label: (e)(ii)
parts.text: State one feature that would be seen, and why, in the proton NMR spectra of each of the two compounds that are not $\mathbf{Z}$.
